{{short description|Square matrix in linear algebra}}
{{For|scattering matrix in physics|S-matrix}}
{{Orphan|date=April 2022}}

In [[linear algebra]], a '''completely-S matrix''' is a [[square matrix]] such that for every principal submatrix ''R'' there exists a positive vector ''u'' such that ''Ru > 0''.<ref>{{cite journal | title = A sufficient condition for the positive recurrence of a semimartingale reflecting Brownian motion in an orthant | first = Hong | last = Chen | journal = Annals of Applied Probability | volume = 6 | issue = 3 | year = 1996 | pages = 758&ndash;765 | url = http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS/Repository/1.0/Disseminate?view=body&id=pdf_1&handle=euclid.aoap/1034968226 | doi = 10.1214/aoap/1034968226| doi-access = free }}</ref>
